patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff does not apply cleanly to the c7131407 vulnerable checkout left by Stage 01, so fixed-side validation uses the real source-level guard from the prebuilt 18066-fix image instrumented at the same source sites. That fixed source contains the expected `if (L == 0) return {};` guard in `permutateAlt()` and the original PoC runs clean there.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First parser-side materialization of the vulnerability-relevant input. Because the outer ruleset selector contains `#{...}`, `parse_ruleset()` takes the delayed selector-schema path and captures the raw selector prefix `4%l:#{&}v,` up to the first `{`, preserving the attacker-controlled trailing comma.

`permutateAlt()` assumes its input vector is non-empty. When `resolve_parent_refs()` passes `vars.size() == 0`, this code underflows `n` to `SIZE_MAX` and allocates a zero-length `state` array without first handling the empty-input case.
Crash site. The first loop test in `permutateAlt()` reads `state[n]` even though `state` has length 0 and `n == SIZE_MAX`, which MemorySanitizer reports as a use-of-uninitialized-value.
Intermediate runtime event resolve_vars materialized from verified transition assertion A-VARS-SIZE-FEEDS-L.

edges.description: The same local `L` computed from `in.size()` at entry is reused unchanged at the sink.
The underflowed index `n = in.size() - 1` is carried unchanged to the later `state[n]` sink.
The empty `vars` vector materialized by `resolve_parent_refs()` is passed unchanged into `permutateAlt()` and becomes the local length `L`.
